advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Align the graph default (and thus the variant string) between verify_completion and verify_completion_start so a default sync/async pair computes the same dedup key.
evidence: async variant: `variant=f"graph={graph};source={source or 'attested'}"` with graph default False (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:355 / signature line ~342)
sync variant: `variant=f"graph={graph};source={source or 'attested'}"` with graph default None (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:469, verify_completion signature graph=None)
compute_key NUL-joins the variant into the sha256 key (src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:117-118)
advisory.finding: The dedup key for verify_completion_start is computed with variant=f"graph={graph};source=..." where graph defaults to the literal False, while sync verify_completion computes the same variant with graph defaulting to None. A default sync call ('graph=None;...') and a default async start ('graph=False;...') therefore produce DIFFERENT keys, so a retry that switches surface (e.g. sync verify_completion times out, agent retries with verify_completion_start) will NOT attach to the in-flight run and launches a second billable pass — the exact double-charge the ticket aims to prevent.
scenarios: Sync verify_completion (default) is in flight; a -32001 timeout prompts a retry via verify_completion_start (default) — the different variant string yields a different dedup key, so no attach and a second billable LLM pass runs.
advisory.suggested_fix: Adopt the tri-state graph=None on verify_completion_start (see prior finding); with identical graph values the variant strings and keys will match.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove the unused module-level logger in _mcp_llm.py (or use it in the daemon/error paths if logging was intended).
evidence: `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` at src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:30
search for 'logger' in src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py returns only the definition line, no usages

scenarios: Reader assumes logging occurs in this module's error paths (e.g. the daemon spawn) when none does.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Write the .rebar/gate_runs/<job_id> index via rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write (tmp + os.replace) so a concurrent gate_status poll never reads a torn/partial record and misreports a live job as 'unknown'.
evidence: Shared mutable resource: the index file `(d / job_id).write_text(json.dumps(record), encoding="utf-8")` at src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:77

Second executor (writer): the background daemon `threading.Thread(target=_bg, daemon=True).start()` at src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:185, whose finally calls `rebar.llm.record_gate_run({... 'status': status ...})` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:172)

First executor (reader): `gate_status` poll runs on a separate MCP worker thread and reads the same file via `raw = (_index_dir(repo_root) / job_id).read_text(...)` at src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:85 (server runs each tool body on its own worker thread — src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:22-29)

Interleaving window: WRITE `write_text` (gate_runs.py:77) overwrites the file the SAME job wrote once as 'running' (record_gate_run is 'Written twice per run', gate_runs.py:66-67); a concurrent READ `read_text` (gate_runs.py:85) landing between truncate and write yields empty/partial JSON

Sibling accessor + its guard: `rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write` — 'temp-in-same-dir + os.replace ... so a concurrent reader / the replayer never observes a torn or partial path' (src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py:1, 14-16); and the peer index writer `llm/workflow/completion_verdict_cache.py:24` 'Atomic writes (tmp + os.replace), last-write-wins safe across concurrent closes'

Harm: torn read -> `except json.JSONDecodeError: return None` (gate_runs.py:90-91) -> `gate_run_status` returns {status:'unknown'} (gate_runs.py:142-143), which gate_status documents as 'job_id is unrecognised' (_mcp_reads.py:222) — a poller can treat a live job as nonexistent and re-fire a duplicate, double-billed *_start, the exact outcome the feature prevents
advisory.finding: record_gate_run persists the shared .rebar/gate_runs/<job_id> index with a non-atomic path.write_text (truncate-then-write) instead of the repo's atomic_write/os.replace discipline used by sibling shared-index writers. Because the daemon thread overwrites the same file (running -> terminal) while gate_status poll threads read it, a poll can read a torn/empty file, decode to None, and report status 'unknown' for a live or just-settled job.
scenarios: A client polls gate_status in a tight loop while the daemon writes its terminal record; the poll reads a half-truncated file, gets 'unknown', and the agent re-invokes review_plan_start believing no job exists.
Two overlapping pollers where one lands during the running->terminal overwrite.
advisory.suggested_fix: In record_gate_run, replace `(d / job_id).write_text(json.dumps(record), encoding="utf-8")` with `rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write(d / job_id, json.dumps(record))` (matching completion_verdict_cache and the other .rebar index writers), keeping the OSError best-effort try/except.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `verify_completion_start`'s `graph` parameter mirror the sync `verify_completion` sibling (`graph: bool | None = None`) to preserve the ticket-type-default tri-state, or document why the async surface intentionally forces `graph=False`.
evidence: Diff adds `verify_completion_start` with `graph: bool = False` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:297)
Sync sibling declares the tri-state: `def verify_completion(ticket_id: str, graph: bool | None = None, ...)` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:411-413)

Sync docstring: `graph` is a tri-state: unspecified (`None`) uses the ticket-type default (an epic verifies its whole subtree; other types verify only their own criteria) (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:425-428)
Behavioral core matches the tri-state: `def verify_completion(... graph: bool | None = None ...)` with 'Default: True for an epic ... else False' (src/rebar/llm/completion.py:290-309)
The new async tool's docstring never mentions `graph`, so the divergence is unexplained (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:295-317)
advisory.finding: On the MCP surface, the new async `verify_completion_start` retypes the `graph` parameter to `graph: bool = False`, diverging from its sync sibling `verify_completion` (and the behavioral core `rebar.llm.completion.verify_completion`), both of which declare the tri-state `graph: bool | None = None` where `None` selects the ticket-type default (epic → whole subtree). As written, an epic verified via `verify_completion_start` defaults to own-criteria-only (graph=False) instead of subtree verification, and the tri-state `None` is unreachable — an undocumented behavioral divergence between two siblings of the same operation.
scenarios: An agent starts completion verification for an EPIC via verify_completion_start: it defaults to graph=False (own criteria only) instead of the sync tool's subtree verification, silently producing a different (weaker) verdict than the sync verify_completion would.
A caller wanting explicit ticket-type-default behavior (None) has no way to request it on the async surface.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change verify_completion_start's signature to `graph: bool | None = None` (mirroring the sync `verify_completion` tool and the core `rebar.llm.completion.verify_completion`), and thread that value through the `variant`/`work` closure unchanged so an epic still defaults to subtree verification.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Make verify_completion_start's graph parameter a tri-state (graph: bool | None = None) matching verify_completion so the async starter preserves the ticket-type default (epic subtree) verification semantics.
evidence: async verify_completion_start signature: `async def verify_completion_start(ticket_id: str, graph: bool = False, ...)`
sync verify_completion signature: `def verify_completion(ticket_id, graph: bool | None = None, ...)` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:411-416)

verify_completion docstring: '``graph`` is a tri-state: unspecified (``None``) uses the ticket-type default (an epic verifies its whole subtree...), while an explicit ``True``/``False`` forces subtree/own-criteria verification — so ``graph=False`` on an epic verifies just the epic's own criteria'
blocking.finding: verify_completion_start declares graph: bool = False, but the sync verify_completion declares graph: bool | None = None where None is a documented tri-state meaning 'use the ticket-type default (an epic verifies its whole subtree)'. The async starter can never pass None, so its default silently forces own-criteria verification (graph=False) on an epic instead of subtree verification — a behavior change from the sync tool the docs present it as mirroring.
scenarios: An agent runs verify_completion_start on an epic expecting the same subtree verification the sync verify_completion default gives; the async starter verifies only the epic's own criteria, producing a weaker verdict.
blocking.suggested_fix: Change verify_completion_start to `graph: bool | None = None` and thread the None through _verify_completion_body/rebar.llm.verify_completion (which already accepts the tri-state).
